article_title: A longitudinal analysis of students' motivational characteristics in introductory physics courses: Gender differences
citation: Emily Marshman, Zeynep Y. Kalender, Christian Schunn, Timothy Nokes-Malach, and Chandralekha Singh. (2017). A longitudinal analysis of students' motivational characteristics in introductory physics courses: Gender differences. https://www.nsf.gov/statistics/2017/nsf17310/data.cfm
title: 29-item motivational survey for introductory physics students
description: A 29-item Likert-scale questionnaire adapted from previously published validated surveys assessing six constructs: fascination with physics, valuing physics, physics self-efficacy, intelligence mindset, grit, and physics epistemology. Items were chosen to "cover the conceptual space of each construct without redundancy" and the survey was designed to be completed in fifteen minutes or less to encourage high completion rates and longitudinal use. Cronbach's alphas were above 0.60 across administrations, and exploratory factor analysis supported six separable scales.
requirements: Administered in written format; online administration in Fall 2015 produced significantly lower participation rates
constraints: Grit subscale was reduced by one item after Fall 2015 because its wording did not correlate well with other grit items
target_learners: undergraduate students in algebra-based and calculus-based introductory physics
target_learning_goals: measuring motivation: fascination, value, self-efficacy, grit, intelligence mindset, physics epistemology
examples: Administered three times over one academic year (Fall 2015 through Spring 2016) in introductory physics courses at the University of Pittsburgh.
